shloka_text: तैर्वध्यमाना देवाश्च ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः । भयार्ताः शरणं जग्मुर्देवदेवं महेश्वरम् ।। 7.6.1 ।।
transliteration: tairvadhyamānā devāśca ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ | bhayārtāḥ śaraṇaṃ jagmurdevadevaṃ maheśvaram || 7.6.1 ||
translation: तैः by them, वध्यमानाः being tormented, देवाः च gods and, ऋषयः च sages and, तपोधनाः whose wealth is penance, भयार्ताः distressed by fear, शरणम् refuge, जग्मुः went, देवदेवम् to the god of gods, महेश्वरम् to Maheśvara.
explanation: Tormented by them, the gods and the sages whose wealth was penance, distressed by fear, went to Maheśvara, the god of gods, for refuge.
comments: The afflicted gods take refuge with Shiva, who, sparing Sukesha's sons himself, directs them to Vishnu, who promises the rakshasas' destruction -- learning of this, the brothers deliberate, and Sumali and Mali, trusting their boons, resolve to attack the gods -- ignoring dire omens the rakshasa host marches on the world of the gods -- Narayana arms himself, mounts Garuda, and the battle opens as the rakshasas assail him.

shloka_text: जगत्सृष्ट्यन्तकर्तारमजमव्यक्तरूपिणम् । आधारं सर्वलोकानामाराध्यं परमं गुरुम् ।। 7.6.2 ।।
transliteration: jagatsṛṣṭyantakartāramajamavyaktarūpiṇam | ādhāraṃ sarvalokānāmārādhyaṃ paramaṃ gurum || 7.6.2 ||
translation: जगत्सृष्ट्यन्तकर्तारम् the creator and destroyer of the world, अजम् unborn, अव्यक्तरूपिणम् having an unmanifest form, आधारम् the support, सर्वलोकानाम् of all worlds, आराध्यम् adorable, परमम् supreme, गुरुम् teacher.
explanation: They went to him who is the creator and destroyer of the world, unborn, of unmanifest form, the support of all worlds, adorable, and the supreme teacher.

shloka_text: ते समेत्य तु कामारिं त्रिपुरारिं त्रिलोचनम् । ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयो देवा भयगद्गदभाषिणः ।। 7.6.3 ।।
transliteration: te sametya tu kāmāriṃ tripurāriṃ trilocanam | ūcuḥ prāñjalayo devā bhayagadgadabhāṣiṇaḥ || 7.6.3 ||
translation: ते they, समेत्य having approached, तु indeed, कामारिम् the enemy of Kama, त्रिपुरारिम् the enemy of Tripura, त्रिलोचनम् the three-eyed one, ऊचुः spoke, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands, देवाः the gods, भयगद्गदभाषिणः speaking with voices choked by fear.
explanation: Having approached Shiva, the enemy of Kama, the destroyer of Tripura, and the three-eyed one, the gods, with folded hands and voices choked by fear, spoke to him.

shloka_text: सुकेशपुत्रैर्भगवन्पितामहवरोद्धतैः । प्रजाध्यक्ष प्रजाः सर्वा बाध्यन्ते रिपुबाधनैः ।। 7.6.4 ।।
transliteration: sukeśaputrairbhagavanpitāmahavaroddhataiḥ | prajādhyakṣa prajāḥ sarvā bādhyante ripubādhanaiḥ || 7.6.4 ||
translation: सुकेशपुत्रैः by the sons of Sukesha, भगवन् O Lord, पितामहवरोद्धतैः uplifted by the boon of Brahma, प्रजाध्यक्ष O Lord of creatures, प्रजाः creatures, सर्वाः all, बाध्यन्ते are tormented, रिपुबाधनैः by their tormenting acts.
explanation: The gods addressed Shiva, saying, "O Lord, O Lord of creatures, all beings are being tormented by the sons of Sukesha, who are uplifted by the boon of Brahma and act as tormentors."

shloka_text: शरण्यान्यशरण्यानि ह्याश्रमाणि कृतानि नः । स्वर्गाच्च देवान्प्रच्याव्य स्वर्गे क्रीडन्ति देववत् ।। 7.6.5 ।।
transliteration: śaraṇyānyaśaraṇyāni hyāśramāṇi kṛtāni naḥ | svargācca devānpracyāvya svarge krīḍanti devavat || 7.6.5 ||
translation: शरण्यानि places of refuge, अशरण्यानि non-refuge, हि indeed, आश्रमाणि hermitages, कृतानि made, नः by us, स्वर्गात् from heaven, च and, देवान् gods, प्रच्याव्य having dislodged, स्वर्गे in heaven, क्रीडन्ति they play, देववत् like gods.
explanation: They have made our hermitages unsafe, and having driven the gods from heaven, they now play in heaven as if they were gods themselves.

shloka_text: अहं विष्णुरहं रुद्रो ब्रह्माहं देवराडहम् । अहं यमश्च वरुणश्चन्द्रो ऽहं रविरप्यहम् ।। 7.6.6 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ viṣṇurahaṃ rudro brahmāhaṃ devarāḍaham | ahaṃ yamaśca varuṇaścandro 'haṃ ravirapyaham || 7.6.6 ||
translation: अहं I am, विष्णुः Vishnu, अहं I am, रुद्रः Rudra, ब्रह्मा Brahma, अहं I am, देवराट् king of gods, अहम् I am, अहं I am, यमः Yama, च and, वरुणः Varuna, चन्द्रः Chandra, अहं I am, रविः Ravi, अपि also, अहम् I am.
explanation: They boast, "I am Vishnu, I am Rudra, I am Brahma, I am Indra, I am Yama, and Varuna, I am Chandra, and I am also Ravi."

shloka_text: इति माली सुमाली च माल्यवांश्चैव राक्षसाः । बाधन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः । तन्नो देव भयार्तानामभयं दातुमर्हसि ।। 7.6.7 ।।
transliteration: iti mālī sumālī ca mālyavāṃścaiva rākṣasāḥ | bādhante samaroddharṣā ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ | tanno deva bhayārtānāmabhayaṃ dātumarhasi || 7.6.7 ||
translation: इति thus, माली Mali, सुमाली Sumali, च and, माल्यवान् Malyavan, च and, एव indeed, राक्षसाः demons, बाधन्ते they torment, समरोद्धर्षाः those who delight in battle, ये who, च and, तेषां their, पुरःसराः leaders, तत् therefore, नः to us, देव O god, भयार्तानाम् to those afflicted by fear, अभयं protection, दातुम् to give, अर्हसि you ought.
explanation: Thus, Mali, Sumali, and Malyavan, along with their battle-eager leaders, torment us; therefore, O god, you ought to grant protection to us who are afflicted by fear.

shloka_text: अशिवं वपुरास्थाय जहि वै देवकण्टकान् ।। 7.6.8 ।।
transliteration: aśivaṃ vapurāsthāya jahi vai devakaṇṭakān || 7.6.8 ||
translation: अशिवं inauspicious, वपुः form, आस्थाय having assumed, जहि kill, वै indeed, देवकण्टकान् thorns of the gods.
explanation: Therefore, assuming a terrible form, indeed destroy these thorns of the gods.

shloka_text: धन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः । इत्युक्तस्तु सुरैः सर्वैः कपर्दी नीललोहितः । सुकेशं प्रति सापेक्षः प्राह देवगणान्प्रभुः ।। 7.6.9 ।।
transliteration: dhante samaroddharṣā ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ | ityuktastu suraiḥ sarvaiḥ kapardī nīlalohitaḥ | sukeśaṃ prati sāpekṣaḥ prāha devagaṇānprabhuḥ || 7.6.9 ||
translation: धन्ते (problematic verb, likely a typo for 'torment' or 'kill'), समरोद्धर्षाः those who delight in battle, ये who, च and, तेषां their, पुरःसराः leaders, इति thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, सुरैः by the gods, सर्वैः all, कपर्दी one with matted hair (Shiva), नीललोहितः blue-red (Shiva), सुकेशं towards Sukesha, प्रति towards, सापेक्षः concerned about, प्राह said, देवगणान् to the hosts of gods, प्रभुः the lord.
explanation: After all the gods had thus spoken about those battle-eager leaders who torment them, Lord Shiva, with matted hair and blue-red form, concerned about Sukesha, spoke to the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: अहं तान्न हनिष्यामि मयावध्या हि ते सुराः । किं तु मन्त्रं प्रदास्यामि यो वै तान्निहनिष्यति ।। 7.6.10 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ tānna haniṣyāmi mayāvadhyā hi te surāḥ | kiṃ tu mantraṃ pradāsyāmi yo vai tānnihaniṣyati || 7.6.10 ||
translation: अहं I, तान् them, न not, हनिष्यामि will kill, मया by me, अवध्याः not to be killed, हि indeed, ते those, सुराः powerful beings, किं तु but, मन्त्रं a counsel, प्रदास्यामि I will give, यः which, वै indeed, तान् them, निहनिष्यति will kill.
explanation: Lord Shiva declared that he would not kill those powerful beings (Rakshasas) because they were invulnerable to him, but he would provide a strategy that would indeed destroy them.

shloka_text: एतमेव समुद्योगं पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः । गच्छध्वं शरणं विष्णुं हनिष्यति स तान्प्रभुः ।। 7.6.11 ।।
transliteration: etameva samudyogaṃ puraskṛtya maharṣayaḥ | gacchadhvaṃ śaraṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ haniṣyati sa tānprabhuḥ || 7.6.11 ||
translation: एतम् this, एव indeed, समुद्योगं plan, पुरस्कृत्य having made primary, महर्षयः O great sages, गच्छध्वं go, शरणं for refuge, विष्णुं to Vishnu, हनिष्यति will kill, सः he, तान् them, प्रभुः the Lord.
explanation: O great sages, taking this very plan as your guide, go seek refuge in Lord Vishnu, for that Lord will surely kill them.

shloka_text: ततस्तु जयशब्देन प्रतिनन्द्य महेश्वरम् । विष्णोः समीपमाजग्मुर्निशाचरभयार्दिताः ।। 7.6.12 ।।
transliteration: tatastu jayaśabdena pratinandya maheśvaram | viṣṇoḥ samīpamājagmurniśācarabhayārditāḥ || 7.6.12 ||
translation: ततः then, तु indeed, जयशब्देन with cries of victory, प्रतिनन्द्य having acclaimed, महेश्वरम् Lord Shiva, विष्णोः of Vishnu, समीपम् to the vicinity, आजग्मुः they came, निशाचरभयार्दिताः afflicted by fear of night-wanderers.
explanation: Then, indeed, those afflicted by the fear of night-wanderers (Rakshasas) acclaimed Lord Shiva with cries of victory and approached Lord Vishnu.

shloka_text: शङ्खचक्रधरं देवं प्रणम्य बहुमान्य च । ऊचुः सम्भ्रान्तवद्वाक्यं सुकेशतनयान्प्रति ।। 7.6.13 ।।
transliteration: śaṅkhacakradharaṃ devaṃ praṇamya bahumānya ca | ūcuḥ sambhrāntavadvākyaṃ sukeśatanayānprati || 7.6.13 ||
translation: शङ्खचक्रधरं bearing the conch and discus, देवं the god, प्रणम्य having bowed down, बहुमान्य having greatly honored, च and, ऊचुः they spoke, सम्भ्रान्तवत् as if bewildered, वाक्यं words, सुकेशतनयान् regarding the sons of Sukesha, प्रति towards.
explanation: Having bowed down and greatly honored the god bearing the conch and discus, they spoke agitatedly concerning the sons of Sukesha.

shloka_text: सुकेशतनयैर्देव त्रिभिस्त्रेताग्निसन्निभैः । आक्रम्य वरदानेन स्थानान्यपहृतानि नः ।। 7.6.14 ।।
transliteration: sukeśatanayairdeva tribhistretāgnisannibhaiḥ | ākramya varadānena sthānānyapahṛtāni naḥ || 7.6.14 ||
translation: सुकेशतनयैः by the sons of Sukesha, देव O Lord, त्रिभिः by the three, त्रेताग्निसन्निभैः resembling the three sacred fires, आक्रम्य having overpowered, वरदानेन by the boon, स्थानानि places, अपहृतानि have been taken away, नः our.
explanation: O Lord, our abodes have been seized and taken away by the three sons of Sukesha, who resemble the three sacred fires, by virtue of a boon.

shloka_text: लङ्का नाम पुरी दुर्गा त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिता । तत्र स्थिताः प्रबाधन्ते सर्वान्नः क्षणदाचराः ।। 7.6.15 ।।
transliteration: laṅkā nāma purī durgā trikūṭaśikhare sthitā | tatra sthitāḥ prabādhante sarvānnaḥ kṣaṇadācarāḥ || 7.6.15 ||
translation: लङ्का Lanka, नाम named, पुरी city, दुर्गा impregnable, त्रिकूटशिखरे on the peak of Trikuta, स्थिता situated, । तत्र there, स्थिताः those who reside, प्रबाधन्ते torment, सर्वान् all, नः us, क्षणदाचराः night-wanderers (Rakshasas) ।।
explanation: There is an impregnable city named Lanka, situated on the peak of Trikuta mountain, where night-roaming Rakshasas reside and torment all of us.

shloka_text: स त्वमस्मद्धितार्थाय जहि तान्मधुसूदन । शरणं त्वां वयं प्राप्ता गतिर्भव सुरेश्वर ।। 7.6.16 ।।
transliteration: sa tvamasmaddhitārthāya jahi tānmadhusūdana | śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ vayaṃ prāptā gatirbhava sureśvara || 7.6.16 ||
translation: सः that, त्वम् you, अस्मत् our, हितार्थाय for the welfare, जहि destroy, तान् them, मधुसूदन O Madhusudana, । शरणम् refuge, त्वाम् you, वयम् we, प्राप्ताः have attained, गतिः protector, भव be, सुरेश्वर O Lord of gods ।।
explanation: O Madhusudana, for our welfare, you must destroy them; we have sought refuge in you, so be our protector, O Lord of gods.

shloka_text: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलान्निवेदय यमाय वै । भयेष्वभयदो ऽस्माकं नान्यो ऽस्ति भवता विना ।। 7.6.17 ।।
transliteration: cakrakṛttāsyakamalānnivedaya yamāya vai | bhayeṣvabhayado 'smākaṃ nānyo 'sti bhavatā vinā || 7.6.17 ||
translation: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलान् whose lotus-like faces are severed by your discus, निवेदय offer, यमाय to Yama, वै indeed, । भयेषु in fears, अभयदः giver of fearlessness, अस्माकम् to us, न not, अन्यः another, अस्ति is, भवता by you, विना without ।।
explanation: Offer to Yama those whose lotus-like faces are severed by your discus, for there is no other giver of fearlessness to us in times of fear except you.

shloka_text: राक्षसान्समरे दुष्टान्सानुबन्धान्मदोद्धतान् । नुदं त्वं नो भयं देव नीहारमिव भास्करः ।। 7.6.18 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasānsamare duṣṭānsānubandhānmadoddhatān | nudaṃ tvaṃ no bhayaṃ deva nīhāramiva bhāskaraḥ || 7.6.18 ||
translation: राक्षसान् Rakshasas, समरे in battle, दुष्टान् wicked, सानुबन्धान् along with their followers, मदोद्धतान् arrogant due to pride, । नुदम् dispel, त्वम् you, नः our, भयम् fear, देव O God, नीहारम् mist, इव like, भास्करः the sun ।।
explanation: O God, just as the sun dispels mist, you should dispel our fear by destroying these wicked, arrogant Rakshasas and their followers in battle.

shloka_text: इत्येवं दैवतैरुक्तो देवदेवो जनार्दनः । अभयं भयदो ऽरीणां दत्त्वा देवानुवाच ह ।। 7.6.19 ।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ daivatairukto devadevo janārdanaḥ | abhayaṃ bhayado 'rīṇāṃ dattvā devānuvāca ha || 7.6.19 ||
translation: इति thus, एवम् indeed, दैवतैः by the gods, उक्तः spoken to, देवदेवः the God of gods, जनार्दनः Janardana (Vishnu), । अभयम् fearlessness, भयदः giver of fear, अरीणाम् to enemies, दत्त्वा having given, देवान् to the gods, उवाच spoke, ह indeed ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the gods, Janardana, the God of gods, who grants fearlessness to his devotees and fear to his enemies, indeed spoke to the gods after granting them protection.

shloka_text: सुकेशं राक्षसं जाने ईशानवरदर्पितम् । तांश्चास्य तनयाञ्जाने येषां ज्येष्ठः स माल्यवान् ।। 7.6.20 ।।
transliteration: sukeśaṃ rākṣasaṃ jāne īśānavaradarpitam | tāṃścāsya tanayāñjāne yeṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ sa mālyavān || 7.6.20 ||
translation: सुकेशं Sukesha, राक्षसं the demon, जाने I know, ईशानवरदर्पितम् proud due to the boon from Ishana (Shiva), ताम्श्चास्य and his, तनयान् sons, जाने I know, येषां among whom, ज्येष्ठः the eldest, स he, माल्यवान् is Malyavan.
explanation: I know the demon Sukesha, who is arrogant due to a boon from Shiva, and I also know his sons, among whom Malyavan is the eldest.

shloka_text: तानहं समतिक्रान्तमर्यादान्राक्षसाधमान् । निहनिष्यामि सङ्क्रुद्धः सुरा भवत विज्वराः ।। 7.6.21 ।।
transliteration: tānahaṃ samatikrāntamaryādānrākṣasādhamān | nihaniṣyāmi saṅkruddhaḥ surā bhavata vijvarāḥ || 7.6.21 ||
translation: तान् those, अहम् I, समतिक्रान्तमर्यादान् who have transgressed limits, राक्षसाधमान् vile demons, निहनिष्यामि will kill, सङ्क्रुद्धः being very angry, सुराः O gods, भवत become, विज्वराः free from fear/anxiety.
explanation: I, being exceedingly angry, will kill those vile demons who have transgressed all limits; therefore, O gods, be free from fear.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तास्ते सुराः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । यथावासं ययुर्हृष्टाः प्रशंसन्तो जनार्दनम् ।। 7.6.22 ।।
transliteration: ityuktāste surāḥ sarve viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā | yathāvāsaṃ yayurhṛṣṭāḥ praśaṃsanto janārdanam || 7.6.22 ||
translation: इति thus, उक्ताः spoken to, ते those, सुराः gods, सर्वे all, विष्णुना by Vishnu, प्रभविष्णुना the all-powerful, यथावासम् to their respective abodes, ययुः went, हृष्टाः delighted, प्रशंसन्तः praising, जनार्दनम् Janardana (Vishnu).
explanation: Thus addressed by the all-powerful Vishnu, all the gods, delighted, returned to their respective abodes, praising Janardana.

shloka_text: विबुधानां समुद्योगं माल्यवांस्तु निशाचरः । श्रुत्वा तौ भ्रातरौ वीराविदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.6.23 ।।
transliteration: vibudhānāṃ samudyogaṃ mālyavāṃstu niśācaraḥ | śrutvā tau bhrātarau vīrāvidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.6.23 ||
translation: विबुधानाम् of the gods, समुद्योगम् the concerted effort/preparation, माल्यवान् Malyavan, तु indeed, निशाचरः the night-wanderer (demon), श्रुत्वा having heard, तौ to those two, भ्रातरौ brothers, वीरौ brave ones, इदम् this, वचनम् word/speech, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Malyavan, the demon, having heard of the gods' concerted effort, spoke these words to his two brave brothers.

shloka_text: अमरा ऋषयश्चैव सङ्गम्य किल शकरम् । अस्मद्वधं परीप्सन्त इदं वचनमब्रुवन् ।। 7.6.24 ।।
transliteration: amarā ṛṣayaścaiva saṅgamya kila śakaram | asmadvadhaṃ parīpsanta idaṃ vacanamabruvan || 7.6.24 ||
translation: अमराः the immortals (gods), ऋषयः and the sages, च and, एव indeed, सङ्गम्य having met, किल it is said, शकरम् Shankara (Shiva), अस्मद्वधम् our destruction, परीप्सन्तः desiring, इदम् this, वचनम् word/speech, अब्रुवन् spoke.
explanation: It is said that the gods and sages, having met Shankara, spoke these words, desiring our destruction.

shloka_text: सुकेशतनया देव वरदानबलोद्धताः । बाधन्ते ऽस्मान्समुद्दृप्ता घोररूपाः पदे पदे ।। 7.6.25 ।।
transliteration: sukeśatanayā deva varadānabaloddhatāḥ | bādhante 'smānsamuddṛptā ghorarūpāḥ pade pade || 7.6.25 ||
translation: सुकेशतनयाः sons of Sukesha, देव O god, वरदानबलोद्धताः arrogant due to the strength of boons, बाधन्ते they harass, अस्मान् us, समुद्दृप्ताः exceedingly arrogant, घोररूपाः of terrible form, पदे पदे at every step.
explanation: O god, the sons of Sukesha, who are exceedingly arrogant due to the power of boons and possess terrible forms, harass us at every step.

shloka_text: राक्षसैरभिभूताः स्म न शक्ताः स्म प्रजापते । स्वेषु सद्मसु संस्थातुं भयात्तेषां दुरात्मनाम् ।। 7.6.26 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasairabhibhūtāḥ sma na śaktāḥ sma prajāpate | sveṣu sadmasu saṃsthātuṃ bhayātteṣāṃ durātmanām || 7.6.26 ||
translation: राक्षसैः by the Rakshasas, अभिभूताः overcome, स्म we are, न not, शक्ताः able, स्म we are, प्रजापते O Prajapati, स्वेषु in our own, सद्मसु abodes, संस्थातुम् to stay, भयात् due to fear, तेषाम् of those, दुरात्मनाम् wicked ones.
explanation: O Prajapati, we are overcome by these Rakshasas and are unable to remain in our own abodes due to fear of those wicked beings.

shloka_text: तदस्माकं हितार्थाय जहि तांश्च त्रिलोचन । राक्षसान्हुङ्कृतेनैव दह प्रदहतां वर ।। 7.6.27 ।।
transliteration: tadasmākaṃ hitārthāya jahi tāṃśca trilocana | rākṣasānhuṅkṛtenaiva daha pradahatāṃ vara || 7.6.27 ||
translation: तत् therefore, अस्माकम् our, हितार्थाय for the sake of welfare, जहि destroy, तांश्च and those, त्रिलोचन O three-eyed one, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, हुङ्कृतेनैव merely with a roar, दह burn, प्रदहताम् of those who burn, वर O best.
explanation: Therefore, O three-eyed one, for our welfare, destroy those Rakshasas and burn them merely with a roar, O best among those who can burn.

shloka_text: इत्येवं त्रिदशैरुक्तो निशम्यान्धकसूदनः । शिरः करं च धुन्वान इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.6.28 ।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ tridaśairukto niśamyāndhakasūdanaḥ | śiraḥ karaṃ ca dhunvāna idaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.6.28 ||
translation: इत्येवम् thus, त्रिदशैः by the gods, उक्तः spoken to, निशम्य having heard, अन्धकसूदनः the destroyer of Andhaka, शिरः head, करम् hand, च and, धुन्वानः shaking, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having thus been addressed by the gods and having heard their plea, the destroyer of Andhaka (Shiva), shaking his head and hand, spoke these words.

shloka_text: अवध्या मम ते देवाः सुकेशतनया रणे । मन्त्रं तु वः प्रदास्यामि यस्तान्वै निहनिष्यति ।। 7.6.29 ।।
transliteration: avadhyā mama te devāḥ sukeśatanayā raṇe | mantraṃ tu vaḥ pradāsyāmi yastānvai nihaniṣyati || 7.6.29 ||
translation: अवध्याः not to be killed, मम by me, ते those, देवाः O gods, सुकेशतनयाः sons of Sukesha, रणे in battle, मन्त्रम् counsel, तु but, वः to you, प्रदास्यामि I shall give, यः who, तान् them, वै indeed, निहनिष्यति will kill.
explanation: O gods, those sons of Sukesha are not to be killed by me in battle; however, I shall give you a counsel (or a plan) that will indeed lead to their destruction.

shloka_text: यो ऽसौ चक्रगदापाणिः पीतवासा जनार्दनः । हरिर्नारायणः श्रीमान् शरणं तं प्रपद्यथ ।। 7.6.30 ।।
transliteration: yo 'sau cakragadāpāṇiḥ pītavāsā janārdanaḥ | harirnārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān śaraṇaṃ taṃ prapadyatha || 7.6.30 ||
translation: यः who, असौ that, चक्रगदापाणिः one who holds discus and mace in hand, पीतवासा wearing yellow garments, जनार्दनः Janardana, हरिः Hari, नारायणः Narayana, श्रीमान् glorious, शरणं refuge, तं him, प्रपद्यथ take refuge in
explanation: You should take refuge in that glorious Narayana, also known as Janardana and Hari, who holds the discus and mace in his hands and wears yellow garments.

shloka_text: हरादवाप्य ते मन्त्रं कामारिमभिवाद्य च । नारायणालयं प्राप्य तस्मै सर्वं न्यवेदयन् ।। 7.6.31 ।।
transliteration: harādavāpya te mantraṃ kāmārimabhivādya ca | nārāyaṇālayaṃ prāpya tasmai sarvaṃ nyavedayan || 7.6.31 ||
translation: हरात् from Hara (Shiva), अवाप्य having obtained, ते they, मन्त्रं the mantra, कामारिम to the enemy of Kama (Shiva), अभिवाद्य having saluted, च and, नारायणालयं to the abode of Narayana, प्राप्य having reached, तस्मै to him, सर्वं everything, न्यवेदयन् submitted
explanation: Having obtained the mantra from Hara and saluted Shiva, they reached the abode of Narayana and submitted everything to him.

shloka_text: ततो नारायणेनोक्ता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः । सुरारींस्तान्हनिष्यामि सुरा भवत विज्वराः ।। 7.6.32 ।।
transliteration: tato nārāyaṇenoktā devā indrapurogamāḥ | surārīṃstānhaniṣyāmi surā bhavata vijvarāḥ || 7.6.32 ||
translation: ततः then, नारायणेन by Narayana, उक्ताः addressed, देवाः the gods, इन्द्रपुरोगमाः led by Indra, सुरारीन् the enemies of the gods, तान् them, हनिष्यामि I will kill, सुराः O gods, भवत become, विज्वराः free from anxiety
explanation: Then Narayana addressed the gods, led by Indra, saying, "I will kill those enemies of the gods; O gods, become free from anxiety."

shloka_text: देवानां भयभीतानां हरिणा राक्षसर्षभौ । प्रतिज्ञातो वधो ऽस्माकं चिन्त्यतां यदिह क्षमम् ।। 7.6.33 ।।
transliteration: devānāṃ bhayabhītānāṃ hariṇā rākṣasarṣabhau | pratijñāto vadho 'smākaṃ cintyatāṃ yadiha kṣamam || 7.6.33 ||
translation: देवानां of the gods, भयभीतानां who were terrified, हरिणा by Hari, राक्षसर्षभौ O best of Rakshasas, प्रतिज्ञातो promised, वधः destruction, अस्माकं of us, चिन्त्यतां let it be considered, यत् what, इह here, क्षमम् appropriate
explanation: O best of Rakshasas, Hari has promised the destruction of us (Rakshasas) to the terrified gods; therefore, let us consider what is appropriate to do in this situation.

shloka_text: हिरण्यकशिपोर्मृत्युरन्येषां च सुरद्विषाम् । नमुचिः कालनेमिश्च संह्रादो वीरसत्तमः ।। 7.6.34 ।।
transliteration: hiraṇyakaśipormṛtyuranyeṣāṃ ca suradviṣām | namuciḥ kālanemiśca saṃhrādo vīrasattamaḥ || 7.6.34 ||
translation: हिरण्यकशिपोः of Hiranyakashipu, मृत्युः the death, अन्येषां of others, च and, सुरद्विषाम् of the enemies of gods, नमुचिः Namuchi, कालनेमिः Kalanemi, च and, संह्रादः Samhrada, वीरसत्तमः the best of heroes
explanation: The death of Hiranyakashipu and other enemies of the gods, such as Namuchi, Kalanemi, and Samhrada, the best of heroes, was also caused by him.

shloka_text: राधेयो बहुमायी च लोकपालो ऽथ धार्मिकः । यमलार्जुनौ च हार्दिक्यः शुम्भश्चैव निशुम्भकः ।। 7.6.35 ।।
transliteration: rādheyo bahumāyī ca lokapālo 'tha dhārmikaḥ | yamalārjunau ca hārdikyaḥ śumbhaścaiva niśumbhakaḥ || 7.6.35 ||
translation: राधेयो Radheya, बहुमायी one with many illusions, च and, लोकपालो Lokapala, अथ and, धार्मिकः Dharmika, यमलार्जुनौ Yamala and Arjuna, च and, हार्दिक्यः Hardikya, शुम्भश्चैव Shumbha and, निशुम्भकः Nishumbhaka.
explanation: This verse lists several powerful and deceitful Asuras, including Radheya, Bahumayi, Lokapala, Dharmika, Yamala and Arjuna, Hardikya, Shumbha, and Nishumbhaka.

shloka_text: असुरा दानवाश्चैव सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः । सर्वे समरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्ते ऽपराजिताः ।। 7.6.36 ।।
transliteration: asurā dānavāścaiva sattvavanto mahābalāḥ | sarve samaramāsādya na śrūyante 'parājitāḥ || 7.6.36 ||
translation: असुरा Asuras, दानवाश्चैव and Danavas, सत्त्ववन्तो endowed with strength, महाबलाः very powerful, सर्वे all, समरमासाद्य having entered battle, न not, श्रूयन्ते are heard, अपराजिताः unconquered.
explanation: All these Asuras and Danavas, though endowed with great strength and power, are never heard to have remained undefeated once they entered battle.

shloka_text: सर्वैः क्रतुशतैरिष्टं सर्वे मायाविदस्तथा । सर्वे सर्वास्त्रकुशलाः सर्वे शत्रुभयङ्कराः ।। 7.6.37 ।।
transliteration: sarvaiḥ kratuśatairiṣṭaṃ sarve māyāvidastathā | sarve sarvāstrakuśalāḥ sarve śatrubhayaṅkarāḥ || 7.6.37 ||
translation: सर्वैः by all, क्रतुशतैरिष्टं hundreds of sacrifices were performed, सर्वे all, मायाविदस्तथा and skilled in illusion, सर्वे all, सर्वास्त्रकुशलाः skilled in all weapons, सर्वे all, शत्रुभयङ्कराः terrifying to enemies.
explanation: All of them had performed hundreds of sacrifices, were skilled in various illusions, proficient in all weapons, and struck terror into their enemies.

shloka_text: नारायणेन निहताः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः । एतज्ज्ञात्वा तु सर्वेषां क्षमं कर्तुमिहार्हथ ।। 7.6.38 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇena nihatāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ | etajjñātvā tu sarveṣāṃ kṣamaṃ kartumihārhatha || 7.6.38 ||
translation: नारायणेन by Narayana, निहताः slain, शतशो by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands, एतज्ज्ञात्वा having known this, तु indeed, सर्वेषां for all, क्षमं forgiveness, कर्तुमिहार्हथ you should do here.
explanation: Knowing that these very beings were slain by Narayana in hundreds and thousands, you should now grant forgiveness to all of them here.

shloka_text: ततः सुमाली माली च श्रुत्वा माल्यवतो वचः । ऊचतुर्भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं भगांशाविव वासवम् ।। 7.6.39 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sumālī mālī ca śrutvā mālyavato vacaḥ | ūcaturbhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhagāṃśāviva vāsavam || 7.6.39 ||
translation: ततः then, सुमाली Sumali, माली Mali, च and, श्रुत्वा having heard, माल्यवतो of Malyavan, वचः words, ऊचतुर्भ्रातरं spoke to their brother, ज्येष्ठं elder, भगांशाविव like Bhaga and Amsha, वासवम् to Vasava (Indra).
explanation: Then, Sumali and Mali, having heard the words of Malyavan, spoke to their elder brother, just as Bhaga and Amsha would speak to Indra.

shloka_text: स्वधीतं दत्तमिष्टं चाप्यैश्वर्यं परिपालितम् । आयुर्निरामयं प्राप्तं सुधर्मः प्रापितः पथि ।। 7.6.40 ।।
transliteration: svadhītaṃ dattamiṣṭaṃ cāpyaiśvaryaṃ paripālitam | āyurnirāmayaṃ prāptaṃ sudharmaḥ prāpitaḥ pathi || 7.6.40 ||
translation: स्वधीतम् well-studied, दत्तम् given, इष्टम् sacrificed, च and, अपि also, ऐश्वर्यम् sovereignty, परिपालितम् protected, आयुः life, निरामयम् healthy, प्राप्तम् obtained, सुधर्मः good dharma, प्रापितः established, पथि on the path.
explanation: We have diligently studied, given charity, performed sacrifices, maintained our sovereignty, attained a healthy life, and established righteousness on our path.

shloka_text: देवसागरमक्षोभ्यं शस्त्रैः समवगाह्य च । जिता द्विषो ह्यप्रतिमास्तन्नो मृत्युकृतं भयम् ।। 7.6.41 ।।
transliteration: devasāgaramakṣobhyaṃ śastraiḥ samavagāhya ca | jitā dviṣo hyapratimāstanno mṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam || 7.6.41 ||
translation: देवसागरम् the ocean of gods, अक्षोभ्यम् unagitable, शस्त्रैः with weapons, समवगाह्य having plunged into, च and, जिताः conquered, द्विषः enemies, हि indeed, अप्रतिमाः unequalled, तत् therefore, नः to us, मृत्युकृतम् caused by death, भयम् fear.
explanation: Having plunged into the unagitable ocean of gods with our weapons, and having conquered unequalled enemies, we therefore have no fear caused by death.

shloka_text: नारायणश्च रुद्रश्च शक्रश्चापि यमस्तथा । अस्माकं प्रमुखे स्थातुं सर्वे बिभ्यति सर्वदा ।। 7.6.42 ।।
transliteration: nārāyaṇaśca rudraśca śakraścāpi yamastathā | asmākaṃ pramukhe sthātuṃ sarve bibhyati sarvadā || 7.6.42 ||
translation: नारायणः Narayana, च and, रुद्रः Rudra, च and, शक्रः Shakra, च and, अपि also, यमः Yama, तथा similarly, अस्माकम् our, प्रमुखे in front, स्थातुम् to stand, सर्वे all, बिभ्यति fear, सर्वदा always.
explanation: Narayana, Rudra, Shakra, and Yama, all of them always fear to stand in our presence.

shloka_text: विष्णोर्देवस्य नास्त्येव कारणं राक्षसेश्वर । देवानामेव दोषेण विष्णोः प्रचलितं मनः ।। 7.6.43 ।।
transliteration: viṣṇordevasya nāstyeva kāraṇaṃ rākṣaseśvara | devānāmeva doṣeṇa viṣṇoḥ pracalitaṃ manaḥ || 7.6.43 ||
translation: विष्णोः of Vishnu, देवस्य of the god, न not, अस्ति is, एव indeed, कारणम् reason, राक्षसेश्वर O lord of Rakshasas, देवानाम् of the gods, एव only, दोषेण by the fault, विष्णोः of Vishnu, प्रचलितम् agitated, मनः mind.
explanation: O lord of Rakshasas, there is indeed no inherent reason for the god Vishnu to act against us; it is only due to the fault of the other gods that Vishnu's mind has been agitated.

shloka_text: तस्मादद्य समुद्युक्ताः सर्वसैन्यसमावृताः । देवानेव जिघांसाम एभ्यो दोषः समुत्थितः ।। 7.6.44 ।।
transliteration: tasmādadya samudyuktāḥ sarvasainyasamāvṛtāḥ | devāneva jighāṃsāma ebhyo doṣaḥ samutthitaḥ || 7.6.44 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, अद्य today, समुद्युक्ताः fully prepared, सर्वसैन्यसमावृताः surrounded by all armies, देवान् the gods, एव only, जिघांसाम we will kill, एभ्यः from them, दोषः the fault, समुत्थितः has arisen.
explanation: Therefore, today, fully prepared and surrounded by all our armies, we shall kill the gods, for the fault has originated from them.

shloka_text: एवं सम्मन्त्र्य बलिनः सर्वे सैन्यसमावृताः । उद्योगं घोषयित्वा तु सर्वे नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवाः ।। युद्धाय निर्ययुः क्रुद्धा जम्भवृत्रबला इव ।। 7.6.45 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sammantrya balinaḥ sarve sainyasamāvṛtāḥ | udyogaṃ ghoṣayitvā tu sarve nairṛtapuṅgavāḥ || yuddhāya niryayuḥ kruddhā jambhavṛtrabalā iva || 7.6.45 ||
translation: एवं thus, सम्मन्त्र्य having deliberated, बलिनः the powerful ones, सर्वे all, सैन्यसमावृताः surrounded by armies, उद्योगं the preparation (for war), घोषयित्वा having announced, तु and, सर्वे all, नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवाः the foremost among the Rākṣasas, युद्धाय for battle, निर्ययुः set out, क्रुद्धा enraged, जम्भवृत्रबला like Jambha, Vṛtra, and Bala (demons), इव as if.
explanation: Having thus deliberated, all the powerful and foremost Rākṣasas, surrounded by their armies, announced their preparations and set out for battle, enraged like the demons Jambha, Vṛtra, and Bala.

shloka_text: इति ते राम सम्मन्त्र्य सर्वोद्योगेन राक्षसाः । युद्धाय निर्ययुः सर्वे महाकाया महाबलाः ।। 7.6.46 ।।
transliteration: iti te rāma sammantrya sarvodyogena rākṣasāḥ | yuddhāya niryayuḥ sarve mahākāyā mahābalāḥ || 7.6.46 ||
translation: इति thus, ते they, राम O Rama, सम्मन्त्र्य having deliberated, सर्वोद्योगेन with full preparation, राक्षसाः the Rākṣasas, युद्धाय for battle, निर्ययुः set out, सर्वे all, महाकाया of huge bodies, महाबलाः of great strength.
explanation: O Rama, having thus deliberated with full preparation, all those Rākṣasas of huge bodies and great strength set out for battle.

shloka_text: स्यन्दनैर्वारणैश्चैव हयैश्च गिरिसन्निभैः । खरैर्गोभी रथोष्ट्रैश्च शिंशुमारैर्भुजङ्गमैः ।। 7.6.47 ।।
transliteration: syandanairvāraṇaiścaiva hayaiśca girisannibhaiḥ | kharairgobhī rathoṣṭraiśca śiṃśumārairbhujaṅgamaiḥ || 7.6.47 ||
translation: स्यन्दनैः with chariots, वारणैः with elephants, च and, एव indeed, हयैः with horses, च and, गिरिसन्निभैः resembling mountains, खरैः with donkeys, गोभी with cows, रथोष्ट्रैः with chariots drawn by camels, च and, शिंशुमारैः with porpoises (or crocodiles), भुजङ्गमैः with serpents.
explanation: They set out with chariots, elephants, mountain-like horses, donkeys, cows, camel-drawn chariots, porpoises, and serpents.

shloka_text: मकरैः कच्छपैर्मीनैर्विहङ्गैर्गरुडोपमैः । सिंहैर्व्याघ्रैर्वराहैश्च सृमरैश्चमरैरपि ।। 7.6.48 ।।
transliteration: makaraiḥ kacchapairmīnairvihaṅgairgaruḍopamaiḥ | siṃhairvyāghrairvarāhaiśca sṛmaraiścamarairapi || 7.6.48 ||
translation: मकरैः with crocodiles, कच्छपैः with tortoises, मीनैर with fish, विहङ्गैः with birds, गरुडोपमैः resembling Garuḍa, सिंहैः with lions, व्याघ्रैः with tigers, वराहैः with boars, च and, सृमरैः with antelopes (or a type of deer), चमरैः with yaks, अपि also.
explanation: They also advanced with crocodiles, tortoises, fish, birds resembling Garuḍa, lions, tigers, boars, antelopes, and yaks.

shloka_text: त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गताः सर्वे राक्षसा बलगर्विताः । प्रयाता देवलोकाय योद्धुं दैवतशत्रवः ।। 7.6.49 ।।
transliteration: tyaktvā laṅkāṃ gatāḥ sarve rākṣasā balagarvitāḥ | prayātā devalokāya yoddhuṃ daivataśatravaḥ || 7.6.49 ||
translation: त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, लङ्कां Lanka, गताः went, सर्वे all, राक्षसाः the Rākṣasas, बलगर्विताः proud of their strength, प्रयाता set out, देवलोकाय for the world of gods, योद्धुं to fight, दैवतशत्रवः the enemies of the gods.
explanation: All the Rākṣasas, proud of their strength and enemies of the gods, abandoned Lanka and set out for the world of the gods to fight.

shloka_text: लङ्काविपर्ययं दृष्ट्वा यानि लङ्कालयान्यथ । भूतानि भयदर्शीनि विमनस्कानि सर्वशः ।। 7.6.50 ।।
transliteration: laṅkāviparyayaṃ dṛṣṭvā yāni laṅkālayānyatha | bhūtāni bhayadarśīni vimanaskāni sarvaśaḥ || 7.6.50 ||
translation: लङ्काविपर्ययम् Lanka's destruction, दृष्ट्वा having seen, यानि which, लङ्कालयानि dwelling in Lanka, अथ and, भूतानि beings, भयदर्शीनि fearful, विमनस्कानि dejected, सर्वशः completely,
explanation: Seeing the impending destruction of Lanka, all the beings dwelling there became utterly fearful and disheartened.

shloka_text: रथोत्तमैरुह्यमानाः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.6.51 ।।
transliteration: rathottamairuhyamānāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ || 7.6.51 ||
translation: रथोत्तमैः by excellent chariots, उह्यमानाः being carried, शतशः by hundreds, अथ and, सहस्रशः by thousands,
explanation: Hundreds and thousands of them were being carried by excellent chariots.

shloka_text: प्रयाता राक्षसास्तूर्णं देवलोकं प्रयत्नतः । रक्षसामेव मार्गेण दैवतान्यपचक्रमुः ।। 7.6.52 ।।
transliteration: prayātā rākṣasāstūrṇaṃ devalokaṃ prayatnataḥ | rakṣasāmeva mārgeṇa daivatānyapacakramuḥ || 7.6.52 ||
translation: प्रयाताः departed, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, तूर्णं quickly, देवलोकं to the world of gods, प्रयत्नतः with effort, रक्षसाम् of the Rakshasas, एव indeed, मार्गेण by the path, दैवतानि deities, अपचक्रमुः departed,
explanation: The Rakshasas quickly departed to the world of gods with great effort, and even the deities departed by the very path used by the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: भौमाश्चैवान्तरिक्षाश्च कालाज्ञप्ता भयावहाः । उत्पाता राक्षसेन्द्राणामभावाय समुत्थिताः ।। 7.6.53 ।।
transliteration: bhaumāścaivāntarikṣāśca kālājñaptā bhayāvahāḥ | utpātā rākṣasendrāṇāmabhāvāya samutthitāḥ || 7.6.53 ||
translation: भौमाः earthly, च and, एव indeed, आन्तरिक्षाः atmospheric, च and, कालाज्ञप्ताः commanded by time, भयावहाः terrifying, उत्पाताः portents, राक्षसेन्द्राणाम् for the chief Rakshasas, अभावाय for destruction, समुत्थिताः arose,
explanation: Terrifying earthly and atmospheric portents, commanded by fate, arose for the destruction of the chief Rakshasas.

shloka_text: अस्थीनि मेघा ववृषुरुष्णं शोणितमेव च । वेलां समुद्राश्चोत्क्रान्ताश्चेलुश्चाप्यथ भूधराः ।। 7.6.54 ।।
transliteration: asthīni meghā vavṛṣuruṣṇaṃ śoṇitameva ca | velāṃ samudrāścotkrāntāśceluścāpyatha bhūdharāḥ || 7.6.54 ||
translation: अस्थीनि bones, मेघाः clouds, ववृषुः rained, उष्णं hot, शोणितम् blood, एव indeed, च and, वेलां the shore, समुद्राः oceans, च and, उत्क्रान्ताः transgressed, चेलुः trembled, च and, अपि also, अथ then, भूधराः mountains,
explanation: Clouds rained bones and hot blood, oceans overflowed their shores, and mountains also trembled.

shloka_text: अट्टहासान्विमुञ्चन्तो घननादसमस्वनाः । वाश्यन्त्यश्च शिवास्तत्र दारुणं घोरदर्शनाः ।। 7.6.55 ।।
transliteration: aṭṭahāsānvimuñcanto ghananādasamasvanāḥ | vāśyantyaśca śivāstatra dāruṇaṃ ghoradarśanāḥ || 7.6.55 ||
translation: अट्टहासान् loud laughs, विमुञ्चन्तः emitting, घननादसमस्वनाः having sounds like thunder, वाश्यन्त्यश्च and howling, शिवाः jackals, तत्र there, दारुणं terrible, घोरदर्शनाः frightful to behold.
explanation: There, jackals, frightful to behold and making terrible, thunder-like sounds and loud roars, were howling.

shloka_text: सम्पतन्त्यथ भूतानि दृश्यन्ते च यथाक्रमम् । गृध्रचक्रं महच्चात्र ज्वलनोद्गारिभिर्मुखैः ।। 7.6.56 ।।
transliteration: sampatantyatha bhūtāni dṛśyante ca yathākramam | gṛdhracakraṃ mahaccātra jvalanodgāribhirmukhaiḥ || 7.6.56 ||
translation: सम्पतन्त्यथ then appearing, भूतानि spirits, दृश्यन्ते are seen, च and, यथाक्रमम् successively, गृध्रचक्रं a flock of vultures, महत् large, च and, अत्र here, ज्वलनोद्गारिभिः emitting flames, मुखैः with mouths.
explanation: Then, ominous spirits were seen appearing successively, and a large flock of vultures with flame-emitting mouths was also present.

shloka_text: राक्षसानामुपरि खे भ्रमते ऽलातचक्रवत् । कपोता रक्तपादाश्च शारिका विद्रुता ययुः ।। काका वाश्यन्ति तत्रैव बिडाला वै द्विपादयः ।। 7.6.57 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāmupari khe bhramate 'lātacakravat | kapotā raktapādāśca śārikā vidrutā yayuḥ || kākā vāśyanti tatraiva biḍālā vai dvipādayaḥ || 7.6.57 ||
translation: राक्षसानाम् of the Rakshasas, उपरि above, खे in the sky, भ्रमते revolves, अलातचक्रवत् like a firebrand wheel, कपोताः pigeons, रक्तपादाः red-footed, च and, शारिकाः mynah birds, विद्रुताः fled, ययुः went, काकाः crows, वाश्यन्ति caw, तत्रैव right there, बिडालाः cats, वै indeed, द्विपादयः two-footed.
explanation: Above the Rakshasas, the vultures hovered in the sky like a fiery wheel, while red-footed pigeons and mynah birds fled, and two-footed cats and crows cawed right there.

shloka_text: उत्पातांस्ताननादृत्य राक्षसा बलगर्विताः । यान्त्येव न निवर्त्तन्ते मृत्युपाशावपाशिताः ।। 7.6.58 ।।
transliteration: utpātāṃstānanādṛtya rākṣasā balagarvitāḥ | yāntyeva na nivarttante mṛtyupāśāvapāśitāḥ || 7.6.58 ||
translation: उत्पातान् omens, तान् those, अनादृत्य disregarding, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, बलगर्विताः proud of their strength, यान्ति go, एव indeed, न not, निवर्त्तन्ते turn back, मृत्युपाशावपाशिताः bound by the noose of death.
explanation: Disregarding those omens, the Rakshasas, proud of their strength and bound by the noose of death, continued to advance and did not turn back.

shloka_text: माल्यवांश्च सुमाली च माली च सुमहाबलाः । आसन्पुरःसरास्तेषां क्रतूनामिव पावकाः ।। 7.6.59 ।।
transliteration: mālyavāṃśca sumālī ca mālī ca sumahābalāḥ | āsanpuraḥsarāsteṣāṃ kratūnāmiva pāvakāḥ || 7.6.59 ||
translation: माल्यवान् Malyavan, च and, सुमाली Sumali, च and, माली Mali, च and, सुमहाबलाः exceedingly mighty, आसन् were, पुरःसराः leaders, तेषाम् of them, क्रतूनाम् of sacrifices, इव like, पावकाः fires.
explanation: Malyavan, Sumali, and Mali, all exceedingly mighty, were the leaders of those Rakshasas, just as fires are foremost in sacrifices.

shloka_text: माल्यवन्तं च ते सर्वे माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम् । निशाचरा ह्याश्रयन्ति धातारमिव देवताः ।। 7.6.60 ।।
transliteration: mālyavantaṃ ca te sarve mālyavantamivācalam | niśācarā hyāśrayanti dhātāramiva devatāḥ || 7.6.60 ||
translation: माल्यवन्तं Malyavan, च and, ते those, सर्वे all, माल्यवन्तम् Malyavan (the mountain), इव like, अचलम् a mountain, निशाचराः night-wanderers (demons), हि indeed, आश्रयन्ति take refuge, धातारम् to Brahma, इव like, देवताः gods.
explanation: All those night-wandering demons indeed took refuge in Malyavan, just as gods resort to Brahma, and as one would take refuge in an unmoving mountain.

shloka_text: तद्बलं राक्षसेन्द्राणां महाभ्रघननादितम् । जयेप्सया देवलोकं ययौ मालिवशे स्थितम् ।। 7.6.61 ।।
transliteration: tadbalaṃ rākṣasendrāṇāṃ mahābhraghananāditam | jayepsayā devalokaṃ yayau mālivaśe sthitam || 7.6.61 ||
translation: तत् that, बलम् army, राक्षसेन्द्राणाम् of the lords of Rākṣasas, महाभ्रघननादितम् resounding like the crashing of great clouds, जयेप्सया with the desire for victory, देवलोकम् to the world of gods, ययौ went, मालिवशे under the control of Mali, स्थितम् situated.
explanation: That army of the demon lords, resounding like the crashing of great clouds, went to the world of gods, which was under Mali's sway, with a desire for victory.

shloka_text: राक्षसानां समुद्योगं तं तु नारायणः प्रभुः । देवदूतादुपश्रुत्य चक्रे युद्धे तदा मनः ।। 7.6.62 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃ samudyogaṃ taṃ tu nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ | devadūtādupaśrutya cakre yuddhe tadā manaḥ || 7.6.62 ||
translation: राक्षसानाम् of the Rākṣasas, समुद्योगम् preparation, तम् that, तु indeed, नारायणः Nārāyaṇa, प्रभुः the Lord, देवदूतात् from a messenger of the gods, उपश्रुत्य having heard, चक्रे made, युद्धे in battle, तदा then, मनः mind.
explanation: But the Lord Nārāyaṇa, having heard of that preparation by the Rākṣasas from a messenger of the gods, then set his mind on battle.

shloka_text: स सज्जायुधतूणीरो वैनतेयोपरि स्थितः । आसज्ज्य कवचं दिव्यं सहस्रार्कसमद्युति ।। 7.6.63 ।।
transliteration: sa sajjāyudhatūṇīro vainateyopari sthitaḥ | āsajjya kavacaṃ divyaṃ sahasrārkasamadyuti || 7.6.63 ||
translation: सः He, सज्जायुधतूणीरः with weapons and quivers ready, वैनतेयोपरि upon Vainateya (Garuda), स्थितः situated, आसज्ज्य having put on, कवचम् armor, दिव्यम् divine, सहस्रार्कसमद्युति having the brilliance of a thousand suns.
explanation: He, with weapons and quivers ready, stood upon Vainateya (Garuda), having donned his divine armor that shone with the brilliance of a thousand suns.

shloka_text: आबध्य शरसम्पूर्णे इषुधी विमले तदा । श्रोणिसूत्रं च खड्गं च विमलं कमलेक्षणः ।। शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गखड्गाख्यप्रवरायुधान् ।। 7.6.64 ।।
transliteration: ābadhya śarasampūrṇe iṣudhī vimale tadā | śroṇisūtraṃ ca khaḍgaṃ ca vimalaṃ kamalekṣaṇaḥ || śaṅkhacakragadāśārṅgakhaḍgākhyapravarāyudhān || 7.6.64 ||
translation: आबध्य having fastened, शरसम्पूर्णे full of arrows, इषुधी two quivers, विमले pure, तदा then, श्रोणिसूत्रम् waist-band, च and, खड्गम् sword, च and, विमलम् pure, कमलेक्षणः lotus-eyed (Nārāyaṇa), शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गखड्गाख्यप्रवरायुधान् the excellent weapons named conch, discus, mace, bow (Śārṅga), and sword.
explanation: Then, the lotus-eyed Nārāyaṇa fastened his two pure quivers full of arrows, his pure waist-band, and his sword, along with his excellent weapons: the conch, discus, mace, Śārṅga bow, and sword.

shloka_text: सुपर्णं गिरिसङ्काशं वैनतेयमथास्थितः । राक्षसानामभावाय ययौ तूर्णतरं प्रभुः ।। 7.6.65 ।।
transliteration: suparṇaṃ girisaṅkāśaṃ vainateyamathāsthitaḥ | rākṣasānāmabhāvāya yayau tūrṇataraṃ prabhuḥ || 7.6.65 ||
translation: सुपर्णं Suparna (Garuda), गिरिसङ्काशं mountain-like, वैनतेयम् the son of Vinata (Garuda), अथास्थितः then having mounted, राक्षसानाम of the Rakshasas, अभावाय for the destruction, ययौ went, तूर्णतरं very swiftly, प्रभुः the Lord.
explanation: The Lord, having mounted the mountain-like Garuda, the son of Vinata, swiftly departed for the destruction of the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: सुपर्णपृष्ठे स बभौ श्यामः पीताम्बरो हरिः । काञ्चनस्य गिरेः शृङ्गे सतडित्तोयदो यथा ।। 7.6.66 ।।
transliteration: suparṇapṛṣṭhe sa babhau śyāmaḥ pītāmbaro hariḥ | kāñcanasya gireḥ śṛṅge sataḍittoyado yathā || 7.6.66 ||
translation: सुपर्णपृष्ठे on Garuda's back, सः He, बभौ shone, श्यामः dark-complexioned, पीताम्बरः wearing yellow garments, हरिः Hari (Vishnu), काञ्चनस्य of a golden, गिरेः mountain, शृङ्गे on the peak, सतडित्तोयदो a cloud with lightning, यथा just as.
explanation: Dark-complexioned Hari, adorned in yellow garments, shone on Garuda's back like a lightning-streaked cloud upon the peak of a golden mountain.

shloka_text: स सिद्धदेवर्षिमहोरगैश्च गन्धर्वयक्षैरुपगीयमानः । समाससादासुरसैन्यशत्रूंश्चक्रासिशार्ङ्गायुधशङ्खपाणिः ।। 7.6.67 ।।
transliteration: sa siddhadevarṣimahoragaiśca gandharvayakṣairupagīyamānaḥ | samāsasādāsurasainyaśatrūṃścakrāsiśārṅgāyudhaśaṅkhapāṇiḥ || 7.6.67 ||
translation: सः He, सिद्धदेवर्षिमहोरगैश्च by Siddhas, Devas, Rishis, and great serpents, गन्धर्वयक्षैः by Gandharvas and Yakshas, उपगीयमानः being praised, समाससाद approached, असुरसैन्यशत्रून् the enemies of the Asura army, चक्रासिशार्ङ्गायुधशङ्खपाणिः holding discus, sword, Sharnga bow, and conch in his hands.
explanation: Praised by Siddhas, Devas, Rishis, great serpents, Gandharvas, and Yakshas, he, holding the discus, sword, Sharnga bow, and conch, approached the enemies of the Asura army.

shloka_text: सुपर्णपक्षानिलनुन्नपक्षं भ्रमत्पताकं प्रविकीर्णशस्त्रम् । चचाल तद्राक्षसराजसैन्यं चलोपलं नील इवाचलेन्द्रः ।। 7.6.68 ।।
transliteration: suparṇapakṣānilanunnapakṣaṃ bhramatpatākaṃ pravikīrṇaśastram | cacāla tadrākṣasarājasainyaṃ calopalaṃ nīla ivācalendraḥ || 7.6.68 ||
translation: सुपर्णपक्षानिलनुन्नपक्षं whose wings (of banners) were scattered by the wind from Garuda's wings, भ्रमत्पताकं with fluttering banners, प्रविकीर्णशस्त्रम् with scattered weapons, चचाल trembled/moved, तत् that, राक्षसराजसैन्यं Rakshasa king's army, चलोपलं with moving rocks, नीलः the blue (mountain), इव like, अचलेन्द्रः the king of mountains.
explanation: That army of the Rakshasa king, with its banners scattered by the wind from Garuda's wings, fluttering flags, and scattered weapons, trembled like a blue mountain king with dislodged rocks.

shloka_text: ततः शरैः शोणितमांसरूषितैर्युगान्तवैश्वानरतुल्यविग्रहैः । निशाचराः सम्परिवार्य माधवं वरायुधैर्निर्बिभिदुः सहस्रशः ।। 7.6.69 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śaraiḥ śoṇitamāṃsarūṣitairyugāntavaiśvānaratulyavigrahaiḥ | niśācarāḥ samparivārya mādhavaṃ varāyudhairnirbibhiduḥ sahasraśaḥ || 7.6.69 ||
translation: ततः then, शरैः with arrows, शोणितमांसरूषितैः smeared with blood and flesh, युगान्तवैश्वानरतुल्यविग्रहैः whose forms were like the fire of cosmic dissolution, निशाचराः the night-wanderers (Rakshasas), सम्परिवार्य having surrounded, माधवं Madhava (Vishnu), वरायुधैः with excellent weapons, निर्बिभिदुः pierced, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: Then, the night-wandering Rakshasas, surrounding Madhava, pierced him by thousands with their excellent weapons, which were smeared with blood and flesh and resembled the destructive fire at the end of an eon. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः ।। 6 ।। Thus ends the sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
